findings.evidence: Proof is captured after argument encoding and current-scope check, immediately before native fetch; only successful decoded task snapshots or batch envelopes receive it. It is a conservative same-realm lower bound, not server receipt time.

The fixed wire decoder makes fresh response objects. After full batch shape validation, current-scope validation and per-item success, only the matching pollTaskRuns result inherits the envelope proof; other logical results and failures do not.

The task hook checks authenticated owner before returning its actual snapshot; observeListRead preserves only that result through a shallow requestedAt wrapper. It does not move the deadline observation anchor or certify merged issue/thread deltas.

Existing accepted/onSuccess, exact committed cache identity, superseded/error, weak lifetime, required+held-at-entry+current revisions, owner namespace, visibility and retired persistent-cache checks remain unchanged. Only began can advance from an attached proof after fulfillment.

Session/workspace/generation fences run before and after transport, and prior to individual batch resolution. A changed owner fails the task snapshot check before SWR can receive a proof-bearing wrapper.

Four appended cases execute real Native queue, codec and fetch code with fixture HTTP/socket boundaries, covering single/batch dispatch after readiness and before readiness. Existing test edits only expose and reset explicit fake-socket open control.

limits: This review does not identify the exact cause of any past Native SQL delta.
A live flush that runs before fulfillment can still conservatively revalidate before a later dispatch proof is available.
No claim is made that the patch removes all second task reads or satisfies production/Native query budgets.
No wire, authentication, TTL, measurement-window or threshold changes were introduced by the reviewed four product diffs.
